prompt:
Two workspace admins wrote in the same week.

1. Their workspace is on the Starter plan. An admin had switched on the daily digest email and the activity feed from the feature-settings page (admins may switch these on for their workspace even though the plan does not include them). Right after another admin changed the default status for new issues in the general workspace settings, digests stopped arriving, and the feature-settings page shows both features switched off again.
2. Another workspace had its digest scheduled for 18:00 UTC and required two-factor sign-in. After an admin allowed public projects, the digest started arriving at 07:00 UTC and two-factor sign-in was no longer required. Nobody had touched those settings.

Expected behaviour: saving workspace settings changes exactly the settings that were submitted and nothing else, including the feature switches. Values that are submitted on purpose must still take effect, even when they are 0 (a digest at midnight UTC), false, or an empty list (switching every feature off). Renaming a workspace must not change any of its settings, and one workspace's save must never affect another workspace.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Injected (single root cause, service): the organization service's settings update now 're-validates' the incoming settings with the full organization-settings zod schema before handing them to the repository. That schema has a .default() on every field, so a partial save is expanded to a complete settings object and every field that was not submitted is reset to its default (digest hour 7, flags [], 2FA false, ...), and the repository's merge then overwrites the stored values. Symptoms surface far away: the digest job's hour check, the digest flag evaluation (feature-flag context -> org overrides) and the flags snapshot. Trap: the obvious fix `.partial().parse(...)` does NOT work, because in zod 4 .partial() keeps field defaults (verified); a fix that re-reads only the flag overrides still loses the digest hour; a truthy-merge fails on hour 0 / false / []. Note: the pristine corpus's update-organization Server Action parses the same partial schema, so it has the same latent reset; the hidden test exercises the service (and the repository merge behind it), not the action. An agent that also fixes the schema passes as well. Validation: bug -> tsc 0, visible 617/617; hidden 3/4 fail (the rename-only case passes on the bug too, by design); bug+solution -> hidden 4/4, full 621/621, tsc 0; naive (re-apply stored flag overrides) -> 2/4 fail; naive2 (`.partial()`) -> 3/4 fail; hidden x3 stable.
